name: Refresh a Webflow directory from Google Maps with Bright Data, GPT-5.6 and Slack

parameters.content:
## Refresh a Webflow directory from Google Maps

A directory is only worth visiting while its numbers are true. This reads every listing in a Webflow CMS collection, pulls what Google Maps says about each business today, and writes back only the ones that actually moved.

### How it works

Each week it reads the collection and takes the Google Maps URL stored on every item. Bright Data fetches all of them in one batch. A single listing came back in 36 seconds in testing, which is why this collects by URL rather than searching.

A code step compares what came back against what the CMS holds and keeps only real movement: a rating that shifted by at least `min_rating_change`, a review count that moved by `min_reviews_change`, a changed phone number or website, or a business Google now reports as closed. Everything else is left alone.

A model rewrites the short blurb for the listings that changed, using the fresh numbers rather than inventing any.

The digest goes to Slack either way. With `dry_run` off, the changed items are written back to Webflow.

### Setup

1. Webflow credential, then put your site and collection ID in **Settings**.

2. Field slugs differ per collection, so set `field_maps_url`, `field_rating`, `field_reviews` and `field_blurb` to match yours.

3. Bright Data Web Scraper API key, plus Slack.

4. Leave `dry_run` on for the first run. `publish_live` is separate: off saves to the CMS without pushing to the live site.

### Customize
Optional add-ons sit unwired beside the main chain: keep a Sheets mirror of the directory, mail the report, or archive venues Maps still lists after they have closed.

## 1. Read the collection
Every CMS item carries a Google Maps URL. Custom fields live under `fieldData`, keyed by their own slugs.

## 2. Ask Google Maps
One batch by URL rather than a search. A single listing measured 36 seconds, so this polls until the snapshot lands.

## 3. What actually moved
Fresh rows are matched back by URL, not by position, and only movement past the thresholds counts as a change.

## 4. Rewrite and check
A fresh one line blurb per changed listing, then the guardrails decide what may be written.

## 5. Report, then write
The digest goes out either way. Only listings that cleared the guardrails reach the CMS.

## Optional add-ons
Not wired up. Mirror the directory to Sheets, mail the report, or archive closed venues.

## Field slugs are per collection

`field_rating` and friends are the slugs in your own collection, not Webflow defaults. Webflow rejects an unknown field with `Field not described in schema`, and this node continues on error, so a wrong slug fails quietly. Check them first.
